sentences.text: This annex defines the syntax of TTCN-3 using extended BNF (henceforth just called BNF).
Table A.1 defines the metanotation used to specify the extended BNF grammar for TTCN-3.
Table A.1: The syntactic metanotation
::= is defined to be definition of non-terminal abc xyz abc followed by xyz concatenation
alternative alternative

[abc] 0 or 1 instances of abc optional {abc} 0 or more instances of abc repetition 1 {abc}+ 1 or more instances of abc repetition 2 {abc}#(n, m) n to m instances of abc repetition 3 (...) textual grouping grouping Abc the non-terminal symbol abc non-terminal "abc" a terminal symbol abc terminal
NOTE: The metanotation defined in table A.1 is parsed from left to right.

The metanotation operators have the following precedence, from highest (binding tightest) at the top, to lowest (loosest) at the bottom: Repetition, Optional Grouping Concatenation Alternative Definition
In general all TTCN-3 language constructs (i.e. definitions, declarations, statements and operations) are terminated with a semi-colon (;).

The semi-colon is optional if the language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace (}) or the following symbol is a right-hand curly brace (}), i.e. the language construct is the last statement in a statement block.
In TTCN-3, all comma-separated lists are terminated with a right hand brace (")"), a right-hand curly brace ("}"), a left-hand curly brace ("{") or a semi-colon (";").

In addition TTCN-3 allows optional trailing commas in comma-separated lists with a variable number of items, i.e. an optional comma is allowed immediately before the closing right hand brace (")") or a right-hand curly brace (}) of a list or before the start of the next lexical symbol indicated by a left-hand curly brace ("{") or a semi-colon (";").
TTCN-3 identifiers are case sensitive and shall only contain lowercase letters (a-z) uppercase letters (A-Z), numeric digits (0-9) and the underscore ( _ ) symbol.
An identifier shall begin with a letter (i.e. not with a number and not an underscore).
::=: abc xyz; is defined to be: abc followed by xyz; definition of non-terminal: concatenation
::=: alternative; is defined to be: alternative
::=: [abc]; is defined to be: 0 or 1 instances of abc; definition of non-terminal: optional
::=: {abc}; is defined to be: 0 or more instances of abc; definition of non-terminal: repetition 1
::=: {abc}+; is defined to be: 1 or more instances of abc; definition of non-terminal: repetition 2
::=: {abc}#(n, m); is defined to be: n to m instances of abc; definition of non-terminal: repetition 3
::=: (...); is defined to be: textual grouping; definition of non-terminal: grouping
::=: Abc; is defined to be: the non-terminal symbol abc; definition of non-terminal: non-terminal
::=: "abc"; is defined to be: a terminal symbol abc; definition of non-terminal: terminal

LF - LINE FEED (10)
VT -VERTICAL TABULATION (11)

The characters of the C0 set of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] and of annex A of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] below are denoting newline (end of line).
A single CR(13) character directly followed by an LF(10) character denote a single end of line (i.e. the sequence CRLFCRLFVT denotes 3 lines):
LF - LINE FEED (10)
VT - VERTICAL TABULATION (11)
FF - FORM FEED (12)
CR - CARRIAGE RETURN (13)
Any character or character sequence that is a valid newline is also a valid whitespace.

requirements.subject: ent:bnf
requirements.canonical: The syntax of TTCN-3 IS defined in annex A using extended BNF (called BNF).
requirements.original: This annex defines the syntax of TTCN-3 using extended BNF (henceforth just called BNF).

requirements.subject: ent:syntactic-metanotation
requirements.canonical: The syntactic metanotation of table A.1 IS parsed from left to right.
requirements.original: NOTE: The metanotation defined in table A.1 is parsed from left to right.

requirements.subject: ent:syntactic-metanotation
requirements.canonical: The metanotation operators HAVE the precedence, from highest to lowest: repetition and optional, grouping, concatenation, alternative, definition.
requirements.original: The metanotation operators have the following precedence, from highest (binding tightest) at the top, to lowest (loosest) at the bottom: Repetition, Optional Grouping Concatenation Alternative Definition

requirements.subject: ent:language-construct
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 language construct (definition, declaration, statement or operation) SHALL be terminated with a semi-colon (`;`), except where clause A.1.2 makes the semi-colon optional.
requirements.original: In general all TTCN-3 language constructs (i.e. definitions, declarations, statements and operations) are terminated with a semi-colon (;).

requirements.subject: ent:semi-colon
requirements.condition: the language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace
requirements.canonical: If a language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace (`}`), the terminating semi-colon MAY be omitted.
requirements.original: The semi-colon is optional if the language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace (}) or the following symbol is a right-hand curly brace (}), i.e. the language construct is the last statement in a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:semi-colon
requirements.condition: the following symbol is a right-hand curly brace
requirements.canonical: If the symbol following a language construct is a right-hand curly brace (`}`), i.e. the construct is the last statement in a statement block, the terminating semi-colon MAY be omitted.
requirements.original: The semi-colon is optional if the language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace (}) or the following symbol is a right-hand curly brace (}), i.e. the language construct is the last statement in a statement block.

ambiguity.issue: The explanation 'i.e. the language construct is the last statement in a statement block' narrows the rule to statements, while the rule itself is stated for all language constructs (e.g. the last definition in a module definitions part or the last field of a type body). Chose the broader reading, in which any construct followed by '}' may omit the semi-colon.
readings: A language construct of any kind (definition, declaration, statement, operation) that is directly followed by `}` MAY omit its terminating semi-colon.
Only a statement that is the last statement in a statement block MAY omit its terminating semi-colon when it is followed by `}`.

requirements.subject: ent:comma-separated-list
requirements.canonical: A comma-separated list IS terminated by a right parenthesis (`)`), a right-hand curly brace (`}`), a left-hand curly brace (`{`) or a semi-colon (`;`).
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, all comma-separated lists are terminated with a right hand brace (")"), a right-hand curly brace ("}"), a left-hand curly brace ("{") or a semi-colon (";").

ambiguity.issue: The character ')' is called 'right hand brace'; it is a right parenthesis (table A.2 calls '( )' begin/end list symbols).

requirements.subject: ent:trailing-comma
requirements.condition: the comma-separated list has a variable number of items
requirements.canonical: A comma-separated list with a variable number of items MAY have a trailing comma immediately before its closing right parenthesis (`)`) or right-hand curly brace (`}`), or before the next lexical symbol `{` or `;`.
requirements.original: In addition TTCN-3 allows optional trailing commas in comma-separated lists with a variable number of items, i.e. an optional comma is allowed immediately before the closing right hand brace (")") or a right-hand curly brace (}) of a list or before the start of the next lexical symbol indicated by a left-hand curly brace ("{") or a semi-colon (";").

ambiguity.issue: It is not stated which lists have 'a variable number of items' (e.g. whether formal parameter lists, actual parameter lists or fixed-size record value lists qualify). Chose the reading that every list whose grammar production allows a variable number of items qualifies. Also ')' is called 'right hand brace'.
readings: A trailing comma MAY appear in every comma-separated list whose BNF production allows a variable number of items (e.g. value lists, parameter lists, import lists).
A trailing comma MAY appear only in lists whose number of items is not fixed by a type, e.g. not in value lists of a record type with a fixed number of fields.

requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Arithmetic operator symbols; { }: + / - *

requirements.subject: ent:concatenation-operator-symbol

requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Concatenation operator symbol; { }: &

requirements.subject: ent:relational-operator-symbol

requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Relational operator symbols; { }: != == >= <= < >

requirements.subject: ent:shift-operator-symbol

requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Shift operator symbols; { }: << >>

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-operator-symbol

requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Rotate operator symbols; { }: <@ @>

requirements.subject: ent:string-enclosure-symbol

requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: String enclosure symbols; { }: " '

requirements.subject: ent:wildcard-matching-symbol

requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Wildcard/matching symbols; { }: ? *

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-symbol
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for assignment symbol IS `:=`.
requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Assignment symbol; { }: :=

requirements.subject: ent:communication-operation-assignment-symbol

requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Communication operation assignment; { }: ->

requirements.subject: ent:bitstring-hexstring-and-octetstring-value-symbol
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for bitstring, hexstring and octetstring value symbols ARE `B`, `H` and `O`.
requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Bitstring, hexstring and Octetstring values; { }: B H O

requirements.subject: ent:float-exponent-symbol
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for float exponent symbol IS `E`.
requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Float exponent; { }: E

requirements.subject: ent:list-element-separator-symbol
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for list element separator symbol ARE `,`.
requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: List element separator symbol; { }: ,

requirements.subject: ent:field-reference-symbol

requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Field reference; { }: .

requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Decoded field reference; { }: =>

requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 special terminal symbol for not-implemented identifier symbol IS `???`.
requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols: Not-implemented identifier; { }: ???

requirements.subject: ent:begin-end-block-symbol
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 special terminal symbols for begin/end block symbols ARE `{` and `}`.
requirements.original: Begin/end block symbols; { }

requirements.subject: ent:predefined-function-identifier
requirements.canonical: A predefined function identifier defined in table 15 and described in annex C SHALL be treated as a reserved word.
requirements.original: The predefined function identifiers defined in table 15 and described in annex C shall also be treated as reserved words.

requirements.subject: ent:reserved-word
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 terminal listed in table A.3 (reserved word) SHALL NOT be used as an identifier in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.original: The TTCN-3 terminals listed in table A.3 shall not be used as identifiers in a TTCN-3 module.

requirements.subject: ent:reserved-word
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 terminal listed in table A.3 (reserved word) SHALL be written in all lowercase letters.
requirements.original: These terminals shall be written in all lowercase letters.

requirements.subject: ent:modifier-terminal
requirements.canonical: A special TTCN-3 terminal (modifier) IS an @-symbol directly followed by an identifier.
requirements.original: Additionally, there are special TTCN-3 terminals consisting of an @-symbol, directly followed by an identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:modifier-terminal
requirements.canonical: A special TTCN-3 terminal consisting of an @-symbol followed by an identifier SHALL be written in all lowercase letters.
requirements.original: These terminals shall also be written in all lowercase letters.

requirements.subject: ent:modifier-terminal
requirements.canonical: The identifier part of a modifier terminal CAN be used in combination with the @-symbol, which gives the annotated language element a specific semantics.
requirements.original: NOTE: These terminals can be used in combination with the @-symbol, which results in a specific semantics for the annotated language element.

ambiguity.issue: 'These terminals' grammatically refers to the @-terminals, which already contain the @-symbol; the intended referent is the identifier part (e.g. 'lazy' of '@lazy'). Chose the identifier-part reading.
readings: The identifier part of a modifier terminal (e.g. `lazy`) CAN be combined with the @-symbol to give the annotated language element a specific semantics.
The complete @-terminal (e.g. `@lazy`) CAN be applied to a language element to give it a specific semantics.

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: The identifier part of a modifier terminal (e.g. `lazy`, `fuzzy`, `nocase`) CAN also be used as an ordinary identifier without special meaning.
requirements.original: They can also be used like any other identifier without any special meaning.

ambiguity.issue: 'They' refers to the modifier terminals, but only the identifier part without '@' can be an identifier. Some identifier parts (e.g. 'control', 'default') are themselves reserved words in table A.3, so the statement does not hold for them. Chose the reading that it applies to identifier parts that are not reserved words.
readings: The identifier part of a modifier terminal that is not a reserved word of table A.3 CAN be used as an ordinary identifier.
Every identifier part of a modifier terminal, including `control` and `default`, CAN be used as an ordinary identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:extension-package-reserved-word
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 terminal listed in table A.5 IS used as a keyword inside the TTCN-3 extension packages.
requirements.original: The TTCN-3 terminals listed in table A.5 are used as keywords inside the TTCN-3 extension packages.

requirements.subject: ent:extension-package-reserved-word
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 terminal listed in table A.5 (extension package reserved word) SHALL NOT be used as an identifier in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.original: These terminals shall not be used as identifiers in a TTCN-3 module.

requirements.subject: ent:extension-package-reserved-word
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 terminal listed in table A.5 (extension package reserved word) SHALL be written in all lowercase letters.
requirements.original: These terminals shall be written in all lowercase letters.

requirements.subject: ent:syntax-element
requirements.canonical: Elements of the TTCN-3 syntax (reserved words, identifiers, terminal symbols and literal values) SHALL be separated by whitespace or by special terminal symbols listed in table A.2, according to the TTCN-3 syntax.
requirements.original: The elements of the TTCN-3 syntax (reserved words, identifiers, terminal symbols and literal values) shall be separated by whitespace or by special terminal symbols listed in table A.2 according to the TTCN-3 syntax.

requirements.subject: ent:whitespace
requirements.canonical: Whitespace MAY consist of one or more of the ITU-T T.50 C0 characters HT (9), LF (10), VT (11), FF (12), CR (13) and SP (32) in any combination.
requirements.original: In representing whitespace, any one or more of the following characters of the C0 set of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] and of annex A of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] may be used in any combination: HT - HORIZONTAL TABULATION (9); LF - LINE FEED (10); VT -VERTICAL TABULATION (11); FF - FORM FEED (12); CR - CARRIAGE RETURN (13); SP - SPACE (32)

requirements.subject: ent:newline
requirements.canonical: Each of the ITU-T T.50 C0 characters LF (10), VT (11), FF (12) and CR (13) IS a newline (end of line).
requirements.original: The characters of the C0 set of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] and of annex A of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] below are denoting newline (end of line). LF - LINE FEED (10); VT - VERTICAL TABULATION (11); FF - FORM FEED (12); CR - CARRIAGE RETURN (13)

requirements.subject: ent:newline
requirements.canonical: A CR (13) character directly followed by an LF (10) character IS a single end of line (e.g. the sequence CR LF CR LF VT denotes 3 lines).
requirements.original: A single CR(13) character directly followed by an LF(10) character denote a single end of line (i.e. the sequence CRLFCRLFVT denotes 3 lines):

requirements.subject: ent:newline
requirements.canonical: A character or character sequence that is a valid newline IS also valid whitespace.
requirements.original: Any character or character sequence that is a valid newline is also a valid whitespace.

requirements.subject: ent:modifier-terminal
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 terminals which are modifiers (table A.4) ARE: `@abstract`, `@control`, `@decoded`, `@default`, `@deterministic`, `@fuzzy`, `@index`, `@lazy`, `@local`, `@nocase` and `@nodefault`.
requirements.original: @abstract @control; @decoded @default @deterministic @fuzzy; @index @lazy @local; @nocase @nodefault

requirements.subject: ent:extension-package-reserved-word
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 terminals which are reserved words in extension packages (table A.5) ARE: `apply`, `assert`, `at`, `configuration`, `conjunct`, `cont`, `delta`, `disjunct`, `duration`, `finished`, `history`, `implies`, `inv`, `mode`, `notinv`, `now`, `object`, `onentry`, `onexit`, `par`, `prev`, `realtime`, `seq`, `setstate`, `static`, `stepsize`, `stream`, `timestamp`, `until`, `values`, `wait`.
requirements.original: apply assert at configuration conjunct cont delta disjunct duration finished; history implies inv mode notinv now object onentry onexit; par prev realtime seq setstate static stepsize stream; timestamp until values wait

requirements.subject: ent:newline
requirements.canonical: Only the CR and LF control characters SHOULD be used for newline, because VT and FF may cause problems with some conventional text editors.
requirements.original: NOTE: It is recommended that for newline only the CR and LF and for whitespace only the HT, LF, CR and SP control characters are used as the VT and FF characters may cause problems with some conventional text editors.

requirements.subject: ent:whitespace
requirements.canonical: Only the HT, LF, CR and SP control characters SHOULD be used for whitespace, because VT and FF may cause problems with some conventional text editors.
requirements.original: NOTE: It is recommended that for newline only the CR and LF and for whitespace only the HT, LF, CR and SP control characters are used as the VT and FF characters may cause problems with some conventional text editors.

requirements.subject: ent:union-field-def
requirements.canonical: At most one UnionFieldDef of a UnionDefBody or NestedUnionDef SHALL contain a DefaultModifier (`@default`).
requirements.original: at most one UnionFieldDef of UnionDefBody or NestedUnionDef shall contain a DefaultModifier

requirements.subject: ent:integer-value-or-range
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression of an IntegerValueOrRange in an Enumeration SHALL evaluate to a statically bound integer value.
requirements.original: SingleExpression shall evaluate to a statically bound integer value

requirements.subject: ent:allowed-values-spec
requirements.canonical: The AllowedValuesSpec of a SubTypeSpec SHALL be of the same type as the type or field being subtyped.
requirements.original: AllowedValues shall be of the same type as the field being subtyped

ambiguity.issue: 'AllowedValues' is not a production name (the production is AllowedValuesSpec); 'field being subtyped' also covers the parent type of a SubTypeDef.

requirements.subject: ent:range-def
requirements.canonical: The RangeDef production in a TemplateOrRange SHALL only be used with integer, charstring, universal charstring or float based types.
requirements.original: RangeDef production shall only be used with integer, charstring, universal charstring or float based types

requirements.subject: ent:sub-type-spec
requirements.condition: the subtyped type is charstring or universal charstring
requirements.canonical: When a charstring or universal charstring type is subtyped, a range and values SHALL NOT be mixed in the same SubTypeSpec.
requirements.original: When subtyping charstring or universal charstring range and values shall not be mixed in the same SubTypeSpec

requirements.subject: ent:string-length
requirements.canonical: The StringLength production SHALL only be used with string types or to limit the length of record of and set of types.
requirements.original: StringLength shall only be used with String types or to limit set of and record of.

requirements.subject: ent:string-length
requirements.canonical: Each SingleExpression bound of a StringLength SHALL evaluate to a non-negative integer value, and the upper bound MAY additionally be `infinity`.
requirements.original: SingleExpression and Bound shall evaluate to non-negative integer values (in case of Bound including infinity)

ambiguity.issue: StringLength has no Bound production; 'Bound' denotes the optional upper bound (SingleExpression or InfinityKeyword).

requirements.subject: ent:formal-value-par
requirements.canonical: A FormalValuePar in a TemplateOrValueFormalPar (template formal parameter list) SHALL resolve to an `in` parameter.
requirements.original: FormalValuePar shall resolve to an in parameter

requirements.subject: ent:array-value-or-attrib
requirements.canonical: Within a BaseTemplateBody, the ArrayValueOrAttrib alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of and set of types.
requirements.original: Within BaseTemplateBody the ArrayValueOrAttrib can be used for array, record, record of and set of types.

ambiguity.issue: 'can be used' may be a plain permission or an exhaustive restriction; the parallel rule for CompoundExpression additionally lists set types. Chose the restrictive reading because it is stated as static semantics.
readings: The ArrayValueOrAttrib alternative of BaseTemplateBody SHALL only be used for array, record, record of and set of types.
The ArrayValueOrAttrib alternative of BaseTemplateBody MAY be used for array, record, record of and set of types, and other types (e.g. set types) are not excluded by this rule.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-identifier
requirements.canonical: The ExtendedIdentifier of a SingleTemplateExpression that is followed by an EnumTemplateExtension SHALL refer to an enumerated value with an associated value.
requirements.original: ExtendedIdentifier shall refer to an enumerated value with associated value

requirements.subject: ent:enum-template-extension
requirements.canonical: Each BaseTemplateBody in an EnumTemplateExtension SHALL be an integer template.
requirements.original: each TemplateBody shall be an integer template

ambiguity.issue: The rule says TemplateBody while the EnumTemplateExtension production uses BaseTemplateBody.

requirements.subject: ent:enum-template-extension
requirements.canonical: The limits of each Range in an EnumTemplateExtension SHALL be integer values.
requirements.original: the limits of each Range an integer value

requirements.subject: ent:struct-field-ref
requirements.canonical: The PredefinedType and TypeReference alternatives of a StructFieldRef SHALL be used only for anytype value notation.
requirements.original: PredefinedType and TypeReference shall be used for anytype value notation only.

requirements.subject: ent:struct-field-ref
requirements.canonical: The PredefinedType alternative of a StructFieldRef SHALL NOT be the `anytype` keyword.
requirements.original: PredefinedType shall not be AnyTypeKeyword.

requirements.subject: ent:par-ref
requirements.canonical: The Identifier in a ParRef SHALL be a formal parameter identifier from the associated signature definition.
requirements.original: Identifier in ParRef shall be a formal parameter identifier from the associated signature definition

requirements.subject: ent:index-ref
requirements.canonical: An IndexRef MAY be used for array types and for record of, set of and map types.
requirements.original: IndexRef shall be optionally used for array types and TTCN-3 record of, set of and map types.

ambiguity.issue: 'shall be optionally used' mixes obligation and option; it is unclear whether this restricts IndexRef to these types or merely permits it.
readings: An IndexRef MAY be used for array, record of, set of and map types.
An IndexRef SHALL only be used for array, record of, set of and map types (and, per the next sentence, string types).

requirements.subject: ent:index-ref
requirements.canonical: The IndexRef notation MAY be used for a string element reference inside a charstring, universal charstring, bitstring, octetstring or hexstring value.
requirements.original: The same notation can be used for a string element reference inside an TTCN-3 charstring, universal charstring, bitstring, octetstring and hexstring type

requirements.subject: ent:index-ref
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression of an IndexRef SHALL resolve to a value of integer type.
requirements.original: SingleExpression will resolve to a value of integer type

ambiguity.issue: 'will resolve' is descriptive; and the preceding rule allows IndexRef for map types, whose keys need not be integers. Chose the reading that integer indices are required except for map keys.
readings: The SingleExpression of an IndexRef SHALL resolve to an integer value for arrays, record of, set of and string types, and to a value of the key type for map types.
The SingleExpression of an IndexRef SHALL always resolve to an integer value, including for map types.

requirements.subject: ent:wildcard-length-match
requirements.canonical: A WildcardLengthMatch SHALL be used only when the MatchingSymbol is used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list.
requirements.original: WildcardLengthMatch shall be used when MatchingSymbol is used in fractions of a concatenated string or list (see clause 15.11)

ambiguity.issue: 'shall be used when' can mean that the length attribute is mandatory in concatenations or that it is only permitted there (the second half forbids it elsewhere).
readings: A WildcardLengthMatch SHALL be attached to AnyValue/AnyOrOmit whenever they are used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list.
A WildcardLengthMatch MAY be used only when the MatchingSymbol is used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list.

requirements.subject: ent:wildcard-length-match
requirements.canonical: A WildcardLengthMatch SHALL NOT be used when the MatchingSymbol is not used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list.
requirements.original: and shall not be used in other cases.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-symbol
requirements.condition: the MatchingSymbol is used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list
requirements.canonical: When a MatchingSymbol is used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list, the Complement, ListOfTemplates, Range, BitStringMatch, HexStringMatch, OctetStringMatch, CharStringMatch, SubsetMatch and SupersetMatch alternatives SHALL NOT be used.
requirements.original: In this case, the Complement, ListOfTemplates, Range, BitStringMatch, HexStringMatch, OctetStringMatch, CharStringMatch, SubsetMatch and SupersetMatch productions shall not be used.

ambiguity.issue: 'In this case' may refer to the concatenation context or to the case where a WildcardLengthMatch is present; DecodedContentMatch is not listed.
readings: In a fraction of a concatenated string or list, the MatchingSymbol SHALL NOT be a Complement, ListOfTemplates, Range, BitStringMatch, HexStringMatch, OctetStringMatch, CharStringMatch, SubsetMatch or SupersetMatch.
When a WildcardLengthMatch is present, the MatchingSymbol SHALL be AnyValue or AnyOrOmit (the listed alternatives SHALL NOT be used).

requirements.subject: ent:pattern-char
requirements.canonical: The characters "?", "*", "\", "[", "]", "{", "}", """, "|", "(", ")", "#", "+", "d", "^" and "N" ARE metacharacters for the definition of pattern elements only if they follow the pattern BNF; otherwise they ARE interpreted as normal characters.
requirements.original: Characters "?", "*", "\", "[", "]", "{", "}", """, "|", "(", ")", "#", "+", "d", "^", "N" have special semantics – they are metacharacters for the definition of pattern elements – only if they follow the BNF as defined above, if not they are interpreted like normal characters

requirements.subject: ent:non-special-pattern-class-char
requirements.canonical: The characters "[", "-", "^", "]", "\", "q" and "," ARE metacharacters for the definition of pattern class characters only if they follow the pattern BNF; otherwise they ARE interpreted as normal characters.
requirements.original: Characters "[", "-", "^", "]", "\", "q", ","have special semantics – they are metacharacters for the definition of pattern class characters – only if they follow the BNF as defined above, if not they are interpreted like normal characters

requirements.subject: ent:wildcard-length-match
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression of a WildcardLengthMatch SHALL evaluate to type integer.
requirements.original: SingleExpression shall evaluate to type integer

requirements.subject: ent:bound
requirements.canonical: A Bound SHALL evaluate to type integer, charstring, universal charstring or float.
requirements.original: Bounds shall evaluate to types integer, charstring, universal charstring or float.

requirements.subject: ent:bound
requirements.condition: the Bound evaluates to charstring or universal charstring
requirements.canonical: If a Bound evaluates to type charstring or universal charstring, its string length SHALL be 1.
requirements.original: In case they evaluate to types charstring or universal charstring, the string length shall be

ambiguity.issue: The source text is truncated after 'the string length shall be'; the required length is missing. Chose length 1 (single character), consistent with clause 6.1.2.2.
readings: If a Bound evaluates to charstring or universal charstring, its string length SHALL be 1.
If a Bound evaluates to charstring or universal charstring, its string length SHALL be some other (unstated) value or SHALL be infinity.

requirements.subject: ent:bound
requirements.canonical: `infinity` as a lower Bound and `-infinity` as an upper Bound SHALL be used only for float types.
requirements.original: infinity as lower bound and –infinity as upper bound are allowed for float types only.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-par-assignment
requirements.condition: the formal parameter is a value parameter
requirements.canonical: If an ActualParAssignment assigns to a formal value parameter, the in-line template (TemplateInstance) SHALL evaluate to a value.
requirements.original: if a value parameter is used, an in-line template shall evaluate to a value

ambiguity.issue: 'value parameter' means formal value parameter; 'in-line template' denotes the TemplateInstance of the ActualParAssignment.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-par
requirements.condition: the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type
requirements.canonical: When the corresponding formal parameter is not a template formal parameter, the TemplateInstance of an ActualPar SHALL resolve to one or more SingleExpressions.
requirements.original: When the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type the TemplateInstance production shall resolve to one or more SingleExpressions

ambiguity.issue: 'of template type' is used for a template formal parameter (there is no template type).

requirements.subject: ent:function-instance
requirements.canonical: The parenthesized ActualParList part of a FunctionInstance SHALL be present unless the FunctionRef uses the ControlKeyword and the referenced module control function has no formal parameters.
requirements.original: the part is only optional if the FunctionRef uses the ControlKeyword and the referenced control function has no formal parameters

requirements.subject: ent:pre-def-function-identifier
requirements.canonical: The Identifier of a PreDefFunctionIdentifier SHALL be one of the predefined TTCN-3 function identifiers from Annex C.
requirements.original: The Identifier shall be one of the pre-defined TTCN-3 function identifiers from Annex C of ETSI ES 201 873-1.

requirements.subject: ent:case-insen-modifier
requirements.canonical: A CaseInsenModifier in a PreDefFunctionIdentifier SHALL be present only if the Identifier is "regexp".
requirements.original: CaseInsenModifier shall be present only if Identifier is "regexp".

requirements.subject: ent:done-operation
requirements.canonical: If the PortRedirectSymbol is present in a DoneStatement (`done` operation), at least one of ValueStoreSpec and IndexSpec SHALL be present.
requirements.original: If PortRedirectSymbol is present, at least one of ValueStoreSpec and IndexSpec shall be present

requirements.subject: ent:killed-operation
requirements.canonical: If the PortRedirectSymbol is present in a KilledStatement (`killed` operation), at least one of ValueStoreSpec and IndexSpec SHALL be present.
requirements.original: If PortRedirectSymbol is present, at least one of ValueStoreSpec and IndexSpec shall be present

requirements.subject: ent:template-body
requirements.canonical: The TemplateBody of a ReplyValue SHALL be type compatible with the return type of the signature.
requirements.original: TemplateBody shall be type compatible with the return type.

requirements.subject: ent:template-body
requirements.canonical: The TemplateBody of a ReplyValue SHALL evaluate to a value or template (literal or template instance) conforming to the template(value) restriction.
requirements.original: It shall evaluate to a value or template (literal or template instance) conforming to the template(value) restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:field-reference
requirements.canonical: The FieldReference of a SingleValueSpec SHALL NOT be a ParRef.
requirements.original: FieldReference shall not be ParRef

requirements.subject: ent:extended-field-reference
requirements.canonical: The ExtendedFieldReference of a SingleValueSpec SHALL NOT be a type definition identifier.
requirements.original: ExtendedFieldReference shall not be TypeDefIdentifier

ambiguity.issue: TypeDefIdentifier is not a production of the Annex A BNF; it presumably means an Identifier in the ExtendedFieldReference that resolves to a type (the anytype alternative).
readings: No element of the ExtendedFieldReference of a SingleValueSpec SHALL refer to a type definition (e.g. an anytype alternative selection by type name).
The ExtendedFieldReference of a SingleValueSpec SHALL NOT consist solely of a type identifier.

improper_terms.proper: Identifier referring to a type definition

requirements.subject: ent:array-def
requirements.canonical: Each array bound (SingleExpression) of an ArrayDef SHALL resolve to a non-negative value of integer type.
requirements.original: ArrayBounds will resolve to a non negative value of integer type

ambiguity.issue: 'ArrayBounds' is not a production name; the bounds are the SingleExpressions of ArrayDef (production 424). The comment is placed after ExtendedTypeFieldReference.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-enum-value
requirements.canonical: The ReferencedEnumValue alternative of a ReferencedValue SHALL be used only for referencing enumerated values.
requirements.original: The second option is used only for referencing enumerated values,

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-value
requirements.canonical: A ReferencedValue that does not reference an enumerated value SHALL use the ExtendedIdentifier [ExtendedFieldReference] alternative.
requirements.original: in all other cases, the first option is used.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-enum-value
requirements.canonical: The ExtendedEnumReference of a ReferencedEnumValue SHALL be present if and only if the Identifier refers to an enumerated value with an attached value list.
requirements.original: ExtendedEnumReference shall be present if and only if Identifier refers to an enumerated value with an attached value list

ambiguity.issue: The ReferencedEnumValue production (441) contains ExtendedTypeFieldReference, not ExtendedEnumReference (442, "(" IntegerValue ")"), so it is unclear which syntax the rule controls.
readings: An enumerated value with an attached value list SHALL be referenced with a parenthesized integer value (ExtendedEnumReference), and other enumerated values SHALL NOT.
The optional ExtendedTypeFieldReference of ReferencedEnumValue SHALL be present if and only if the enumerated value has an attached value list.

requirements.subject: ent:char
requirements.canonical: A Char in a charstring IS a character from the character set defined in ITU-T T.50.
requirements.original: A character defined by the relevant CharacterString type. For charstring a character from the character set defined in ITU-T T.50.

requirements.subject: ent:char
requirements.canonical: A Char in a universal charstring IS a character from any character set defined in ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: For universal charstring a character from any character set defined in ISO/IEC 10646.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-alpha-num
requirements.canonical: An ExtendedAlphaNum IS a graphical character from the BASIC LATIN or LATIN-1 SUPPLEMENT character sets of ISO/IEC 10646, i.e. a character from char(0,0,0,32) to char(0,0,0,126), from char(0,0,0,161) to char(0,0,0,172) or from char(0,0,0,174) to char(0,0,0,255).
requirements.original: A graphical character from BASIC LATIN or LATIN-1 SUPPLEMENT character sets defined in ISO/IEC 10646 (characters from char (0,0,0,32) to char (0,0,0,126), from char (0,0,0,161) to char (0,0,0,172) and from char (0,0,0,174) to char (0,0,0,255)

requirements.subject: ent:nl-char
requirements.canonical: An NLChar IS any sequence of the newline characters LF(10), VT(11), FF(12) and CR(13) of ITU-T T.50 that constitutes a newline.
requirements.original: Any sequence of newline characters that constitute a newline by using the following C0 control characters: LF(10), VT(11), FF(12), CR(13) (jointly called newline characters, see clause A.1.5.1) from the character set defined in Recommendation ITU-T T.50.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-field-or-type-reference
requirements.canonical: An Identifier in an ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference refers to a type definition if the type of the referenced definition in which the ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference is used is anytype.
requirements.original: The Identifier refers to a type definition if the type of the VarInstance or ReferencedValue in which the ExtendedFieldOrReference is used is anytype.

ambiguity.issue: The rule names 'ExtendedFieldOrReference' (production is ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference) and VarInstance/ReferencedValue, which do not occur in the DefOrFieldRef context of attribute qualifiers.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-field-or-type-reference
requirements.canonical: An IndexRef SHALL be used in an ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference when referencing elements of values or arrays.
requirements.original: IndexRef shall be used when referencing elements of values or arrays.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-field-or-type-reference
requirements.canonical: The square brackets with dash "[-]" SHALL be used in an ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference when referencing the inner type of a record of, set of or array type.
requirements.original: The square brackets with dash shall be used when referencing inner types of a record of, set of or array type.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: In a function returning a value, the TemplateInstance of a ReturnStatement SHALL evaluate to a value of a type compatible with the return type.
requirements.original: TemplateInstance shall evaluate to a value of a type compatible with the return type for functions returning a value.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: In a function returning a template, the TemplateInstance of a ReturnStatement SHALL evaluate to a value, a template (literal or template instance) or a matching mechanism compatible with the return type.
requirements.original: It shall evaluate to a value, template (literal or template instance), or a matching mechanism compatible with the return type for functions returning a template.

requirements.subject: ent:array-or-mixed-expression
requirements.canonical: Within a CompoundExpression, the ArrayOrMixedExpression alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of, set and set of types.
requirements.original: Within CompoundExpression the ArrayOrMixedExpression can be used for Arrays, record, record of, set and set of types.

ambiguity.issue: 'can be used' may be a permission or an exhaustive restriction; the lists differ from the parallel rules for BaseTemplateBody and CompoundConstExpression (which omit set). Chose the restrictive reading.
readings: The ArrayOrMixedExpression alternative SHALL only be used for array, record, record of, set and set of types.
The ArrayOrMixedExpression alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of, set and set of types, without excluding other types.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-expression
requirements.canonical: A BooleanExpression SHALL resolve to a value of type boolean.
requirements.original: BooleanExpression shall resolve to a Value of type Boolean

requirements.subject: ent:array-const-expression
requirements.canonical: Within a CompoundConstExpression, the ArrayConstExpression alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of and set of types.
requirements.original: Within CompoundConstExpression the ArrayConstExpression can be used for arrays, record, record of and set of types.

ambiguity.issue: 'can be used' may be a permission or an exhaustive restriction; unlike the CompoundExpression rule, set types are not listed.
readings: The ArrayConstExpression alternative SHALL only be used for array, record, record of and set of types.
The ArrayConstExpression alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of and set of types, without excluding set types.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.condition: the left hand side is a value variable
requirements.canonical: When the left hand side of an Assignment is a value variable, the TemplateBody on the right hand side SHALL evaluate to an explicit value of a type compatible with the type of the left hand side.
requirements.original: The TemplateBody on the right hand side of Assignment shall evaluate to an explicit value of a type compatible with the type of the left hand side for value variables

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.condition: the left hand side is a template variable
requirements.canonical: When the left hand side of an Assignment is a template variable, the TemplateBody on the right hand side SHALL evaluate to an explicit value, a template (literal or template instance) or a matching mechanism compatible with the type of the left hand side.
requirements.original: and shall evaluate to an explicit value, template (literal or a template instance) or a matching mechanism compatible with the type of the left hand side for template variables.

requirements.subject: ent:single-expression
requirements.canonical: If a SingleExpression contains more than one XorExpression, the XorExpressions (operands of `or`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.original: If more than one XorExpression exists, then the XorExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types

requirements.subject: ent:xor-expression
requirements.canonical: If a XorExpression contains more than one AndExpression, the AndExpressions (operands of `xor`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.original: If more than one AndExpression exists, then the AndExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types

requirements.subject: ent:and-expression
requirements.canonical: If a AndExpression contains more than one NotExpression, the NotExpressions (operands of `and`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.original: If more than one NotExpression exists, then the NotExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types

requirements.subject: ent:not-expression
requirements.canonical: The operand of the `not` operator in a NotExpression SHALL be of type boolean or a type derived from boolean.
requirements.original: Operands of the not operator shall be of type boolean or derivatives of type Boolean.

requirements.subject: ent:equal-expression
requirements.canonical: If an EqualExpression contains more than one RelExpression, the RelExpressions SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.original: If more than one RelExpression exists, then the RelExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types.

requirements.subject: ent:equal-expression
requirements.canonical: If an EqualExpression contains only one RelExpression, that RelExpression SHALL NOT derive to a CompoundExpression.
requirements.original: If only one RelExpression exists, it shall not derive to a CompoundExpression.

requirements.subject: ent:rel-expression
requirements.canonical: If a RelExpression contains both ShiftExpressions, each ShiftExpression SHALL evaluate to a specific integer, enumerated or float value or a value of a type derived from these types.
requirements.original: If both ShiftExpressions exist, then each ShiftExpression shall evaluate to a specific integer, Enumerated or float Value or derivatives of these types.

requirements.subject: ent:shift-expression
requirements.canonical: Each BitOrExpression operand of a ShiftExpression SHALL resolve to a specific value.
requirements.original: Each Result shall resolve to a specific Value.

ambiguity.issue: 'Result' is not a production name; the operands of ShiftExpression are BitOrExpressions.

requirements.subject: ent:shift-expression
requirements.canonical: If a ShiftExpression contains more than one operand, the right-hand operand SHALL be of type integer or a type derived from integer.
requirements.original: If more than one Result exists the right-hand operand shall be of type integer or derivatives

ambiguity.issue: 'Result' is not a production name; the operands of ShiftExpression are BitOrExpressions.

requirements.subject: ent:shift-operator
requirements.canonical: If the shift operator is `<<` or `>>`, the left-hand operand SHALL resolve to bitstring, hexstring or octetstring type or a type derived from these types.
requirements.original: if the shift op is "<<" or ">>" then the left-hand operand shall resolve to either bitstring, hexstring or octetstring type or derivatives of these types. If the shift op is "

ambiguity.issue: 'Result' is used for the BitOrExpression operands. The text is truncated after 'If the shift op is "' - the corresponding rule for the rotate operators `<@` and `@>` is missing (see clause 7.1.5).

requirements.subject: ent:bit-or-expression
requirements.canonical: If a BitOrExpression contains more than one BitXorExpression, the BitXorExpressions (operands of `or4b`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.original: If more than one BitXorExpression exists, then the BitXorExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types

requirements.subject: ent:bit-xor-expression
requirements.canonical: If a BitXorExpression contains more than one BitAndExpression, the BitAndExpressions (operands of `xor4b`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.original: If more than one BitAndExpression exists, then the BitAndExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types

requirements.subject: ent:bit-and-expression
requirements.canonical: If a BitAndExpression contains more than one BitNotExpression, the BitNotExpressions (operands of `and4b`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.original: If more than one BitNotExpression exists, then the BitNotExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types

requirements.subject: ent:bit-not-expression
requirements.canonical: If the `not4b` operator is present in a BitNotExpression, its operand SHALL be of type bitstring, octetstring or hexstring or a type derived from these types.
requirements.original: If the not4b operator exists, the operand shall be of type bitstring, octetstring or hexstring or derivatives of these types.

requirements.subject: ent:add-expression
requirements.canonical: Each MulExpression of an AddExpression SHALL resolve to a specific value.
requirements.original: Each MulExpression shall resolve to a specific Value.

requirements.subject: ent:add-expression
requirements.condition: more than one MulExpression exists and the AddOp is StringOp
requirements.canonical: If an AddExpression contains more than one MulExpression and the AddOp resolves to StringOp, the MulExpressions SHALL be valid operands for StringOp.
requirements.original: If more than one MulExpression exists and the AddOp resolves to StringOp then the MulExpressions shall be valid operands for StringOp.

requirements.subject: ent:add-expression
requirements.condition: more than one MulExpression exists and the AddOp is + or -
requirements.canonical: If an AddExpression contains more than one MulExpression and the AddOp does not resolve to StringOp, both MulExpressions SHALL resolve to type integer or float or a type derived from these types.
requirements.original: If more than one MulExpression exists and the AddOp does not resolve to StringOp then the MulExpression shall both resolve to type integer or float or derivatives of these types.

requirements.subject: ent:add-expression
requirements.canonical: If an AddExpression contains only one MulExpression, that MulExpression SHALL NOT derive to a CompoundExpression.
requirements.original: If only one MulExpression exists, it shall not derive to a CompoundExpression.

requirements.subject: ent:mul-expression
requirements.canonical: Each UnaryExpression of a MulExpression SHALL resolve to a specific value.
requirements.original: Each UnaryExpression shall resolve to a specific Value.

requirements.subject: ent:mul-expression
requirements.canonical: If a MulExpression contains more than one UnaryExpression, the UnaryExpressions SHALL resolve to type integer or float or a type derived from these types.
requirements.original: If more than one UnaryExpression exists then the UnaryExpressions shall resolve to type integer or float or derivatives of these types.

requirements.subject: ent:unary-expression
requirements.canonical: If a UnaryExpression contains a UnaryOp, its Primary SHALL resolve to a specific value of type integer or float or a type derived from these types.
requirements.original: Primary shall resolve to a specific Value of type integer or float or derivatives of these types.

ambiguity.issue: The rule has no condition, which read literally would restrict every Primary (and thus every expression) to integer or float values; it is only meaningful when the optional UnaryOp is present.
readings: If a UnaryOp is present, the Primary of a UnaryExpression SHALL resolve to a specific integer or float value.
The Primary of a UnaryExpression SHALL always resolve to a specific integer or float value.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-field-reference
requirements.canonical: An Identifier in an ExtendedFieldReference refers to a type definition if the type of the VarInstance or ReferencedValue in which the ExtendedFieldReference is used is anytype.
requirements.original: The Identifier refers to a type definition if the type of the VarInstance or ReferencedValue in which the ExtendedFieldReference is used is anytype.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-field-reference
requirements.canonical: An IndexRef SHALL be used in an ExtendedFieldReference when referencing elements of values or arrays.
requirements.original: IndexRef shall be used when referencing elements of values or arrays.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-field-reference
requirements.canonical: A DecodedFieldReference SHALL NOT appear on the left-hand side of an assignment.
requirements.original: DecodedFieldReference shall not appear on the left-hand side of assignments

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-field-reference
requirements.canonical: A DecodedFieldReference SHALL NOT appear in a type reference.
requirements.original: DecodedFieldReference shall not appear on the left-hand side of assignments and in type references

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-field-type
requirements.canonical: The Identifier of a DecodedFieldType SHALL resolve to a type.
requirements.original: The Identifier shall resolve into a type

requirements.subject: ent:add-op
requirements.canonical: The operands of the binary `+` and `-` operators (AddOp) SHALL be of type integer or float or a type derived from integer or float (i.e. a subrange).
requirements.original: Operands of the "+" or "-" operators shall be of type integer or float or derivations of integer or float (i.e. subrange)

requirements.subject: ent:multiply-op
requirements.canonical: The operands of the `*`, `/`, `rem` and `mod` operators (MultiplyOp) SHALL be of type integer or float or a type derived from integer or float (i.e. a subrange).
requirements.original: Operands of the "*", "/", rem or mod operators shall be of type integer or float or derivations of integer or float (i.e. subrange)

ambiguity.issue: The rule allows float operands for `rem` and `mod`, while clause 7.1.1 restricts `rem` and `mod` to integer operands.
readings: The operands of `*` and `/` SHALL be integer or float (or derived) and the operands of `rem` and `mod` SHALL be integer (or derived), as in clause 7.1.1.
The operands of `*`, `/`, `rem` and `mod` SHALL all be integer or float (or derived).

requirements.subject: ent:unary-op
requirements.canonical: The operand of the unary `+` and `-` operators (UnaryOp) SHALL be of type integer or float or a type derived from integer or float (i.e. a subrange).
requirements.original: Operands of the "+" or "-" operators shall be of type integer or float or derivations of integer or float (i.e. subrange)

requirements.subject: ent:string-op
requirements.canonical: The operands of the concatenation operator `&` (StringOp) SHALL be of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of or array types, or types derived from these types.
requirements.original: Operands of the list operator shall be bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, (universal) character string, record of, set of, or array types, or derivates of these types.

ambiguity.issue: The '&' operator is called 'list operator' here, but 'concatenation operator' in clause 7.1.2; '(universal) character string' is used for charstring/universal charstring.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.condition: the UnionKeyword is present in the surrounding SelectCaseConstruct
requirements.canonical: If the UnionKeyword is present in the surrounding SelectCaseConstruct, each TemplateInstance of a SelectCase SHALL be an Identifier.
requirements.original: TemplateInstance-s shall be Identifier-s if the UnionKeyword is present in the surrounding SelectCaseConstruct (see clause 19.3.2)
